{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1941)}}
'''Anthony William Knapp''' (born 2 December 1941, [[Morristown, New Jersey|Morristown]], [[New Jersey]])<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale</ref> is an American mathematician and professor emeritus at the [[State University of New York, Stony Brook]] working in [[representation theory]]. For much of his career, Knapp was a professor at [[Cornell University]].

==Education==
Knapp lived in [[Baltimore, Maryland]],<ref name="dam-62"/> and graduated from the preparatory [[McDonogh School]] nearby.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-baltimore-sun-marriage-of-adamson/70454207/ | title=To Become Bride Of Mr. Knapp | newspaper=The Baltimore Sun | date=June 2, 1963 | page=78 | via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> He attended [[Dartmouth College]],<ref name="nams-dec97"/> graduating from there in 1962 and receiving a [[ National Science Foundation Graduate Fellowship]] to continue his studies.<ref name="dam-62">{{cite news | url=https://archive.dartmouthalumnimagazine.com/article/1962/6/1/honors-for-62-men | title=Honors for '62 Men | magazine=Dartmouth Alumni Magazine | date=June 1962 | page=39 }}</ref>  Knapp received his Ph.D. in 1965 from [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Salomon Bochner]].<ref name="nams-dec97"/>

== Teaching ==
Knapp began his career as a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] for two years at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]],<ref name="nams-dec97"/> before gaining a position as an [[assistant professor]] at [[Cornell University]] in 1967.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://math.cornell.edu/international-congress | title=Cornellians at the International Congress of Mathematicians | publisher=Department of Mathematics, Cornell University | access-date=June 2, 2024 }}</ref> He was promoted to [[associate professor]] there in 1970 and [[full professor]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~aknapp/vita.html | title=Vita for Anthony W. Knapp | publisher=SUNY Stony Brook | access-date=May 27, 2024}}</ref> Knapp began spending some of his time at [[SUNY Stony Brook]] in 1986 and took a full-time position there in 1990.<ref name="nams-dec97">{{cite journal | url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199711/comm-knapp.pdf | title=Anthony Knapp Appointed ''Notices'' Editor | journal=Notices of the AMS | publisher=American Mathematical Society | date=December 1997 | pages=1457–1458 | first=Allyn | last=Jackson | volume=44 | number=11 }}</ref>

==Research==
In a series of papers from 1976 to 1984, Knapp and [[Gregg  Zuckerman]] gave the classification of [[tempered representation]]s of [[semisimple]] [[Lie group]]s.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Knapp | first1=Anthony W. | last2=Zuckerman | first2=Gregg | title=Classification of irreducible tempered representations of semi-simple Lie groups | jstor=65732 | mr=0460545 | year=1976 | journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] | issn=0027-8424 | volume=73 | issue=7 | pages=2178–2180 | doi=10.1073/pnas.73.7.2178 | pmid=16592331 | pmc=430485| bibcode=1976PNAS...73.2178K | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Knapp | first1=Anthony W. | last2=Zuckerman | first2=Gregg J. | title=Classification of irreducible tempered representations of semisimple groups. Part I | doi=10.2307/2007066 | mr=672840 | year=1982 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=116 | issue=2 | pages=389–455| jstor=2007066 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Knapp | first1=Anthony W. | last2=Zuckerman | first2=Gregg J. | title=Classification of irreducible tempered representations of semisimple groups. Part II | jstor=2007019 | doi=10.2307/2007019 | mr=672840 | year=1982 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=116 | issue=3 | pages=457–501}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Knapp | first1=Anthony W. | last2=Zuckerman | first2=Gregg J. | title=Correction | doi=10.2307/2007089 | mr=744867 | year=1984 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=119 | issue=3 | pages=639| jstor=2007089 }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
He won the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition in 1997.<ref>{{cite journal|title=1997 Steele Prizes|journal=Notices of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199703/comm-steele.pdf}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>
